scenes.text: A hummingbird's heart can beat more than twelve hundred times a minute.
That's about twenty beats every single second.
Their wings beat so fast they make a humming sound, which is how they got their name.
They can hover perfectly still in midair, and they can even fly backwards.
Hummingbirds live only in the Americas, and there are more than three hundred species.
The smallest is the bee hummingbird from Cuba, the tiniest bird on Earth.
It weighs around two grams, lighter than a single dime.
All that speed burns energy incredibly fast, so they have to feed many times a day.
So how do they survive a long, cold night without food?
They slip into a deep, sleep-like state called torpor.
Their body temperature drops, and their heart can slow to around fifty beats a minute.
Scientists think this helps them save a big share of their energy until sunrise.
In the morning, they warm back up and zoom off to find flowers.
Some ruby-throated hummingbirds fly nonstop across the Gulf of Mexico when they migrate.
That's a journey of around five hundred miles, with nowhere to land.
Have you ever seen a hummingbird up close?

title: A hummingbird's heart beats 1,200 times a minute ❤️
caption: Hummingbirds' hearts can top 1,200 beats a minute, but on cold nights they drop into torpor and slow to around 50. Some cross the Gulf of Mexico nonstop!
